label: Person
name: Alberich Mazak
summary:
Alberich Mazak (1609–1661) was a Cistercian bishop who served as Bishop of Celje (Cilli) in Styria, contributing to the Catholic Reformation in the Slovenian-speaking regions of the Habsburg lands. Born in Styria, he joined the Cistercian order and rose through its ranks before being appointed to episcopal office in the Habsburg hereditary lands.

Celje/Cilli's diocese was part of the complex ecclesiastical map of inner Austria, a region where the Protestant Reformation had made significant inroads in the sixteenth century and where the Catholic Reformation was gradually restoring Catholic life through the seventeenth century. Mazak's episcopate contributed to the consolidation of Catholic practice in a borderland region where Lutheran and Catholic communities had coexisted in uneasy tension.

His Cistercian background brought the spiritual resources of his order's tradition of contemplation and learning to a diocese engaged in the demanding work of Catholic recovery. His career exemplifies the role of religious order bishops in the Habsburg implementation of the Catholic Reformation in the eastern Alpine regions, where the counter-reformation success was substantial but required sustained episcopal effort across several generations.
